Include a side-view running dinosaur, layered desert ground, cacti and a flying obstacle, score and high-score HUD, a small speed indicator, and a clear jump instruction. Put strong emphasis on crisp silhouette readability, rhythmic spacing, a distinctive modern-retro identity, and a coherent, highly polished composition rather than a bare clone.

history.critique: Brief & Intent Alignment: Two required elements are simply absent — no cacti and no flying obstacle appear anywhere in the viewport, so the 'desert runner' premise is unfulfilled despite the sunset dressing. The dinosaur is present but rendered as a ~20px dark blob with two stray yellow pixels (eyes) that read as glitches, directly violating the brief's core emphasis on crisp silhouette readability. The 'running' state is static. The jump instruction exists but is muddled: two jump chips (SPACE and r) with a contradictory down-arrow on 'r Jump'. Clarity & Hierarchy: Focal priority is inverted — the glowing sun is the visual anchor, not the player. The score/high-score HUD is duplicated (header chips AND an in-canvas HUD), splitting attention and forcing the viewer to guess which is canonical; the in-canvas copy also collides with the sun's glow. The 'RIPOSA · RUN' watermark is low-value noise, and 'VELOCITY 0.0× base' is a cryptic debug label detached from the action. Visual System & Craft: The soft bokeh cloud blobs look like out-of-focus rendering artifacts and break the crisp modern-retro identity; the dashed ground line reads as a road/track rather than desert; the ground below is muddy purple noise instead of layered sand. Two competing type systems (header monospace vs in-canvas pixel numerals) and two competing HUD locations fragment the system. The dino's feet don't sit on a confident ground plane. Expressiveness & Distinctiveness: The scene is empty and static — no obstacles, no parallax rhythm, no motion cues, no memorable moment — so 'RIPOSA' remains a label rather than an identity; the purple/orange sunset plus bokeh is a generic placeholder look. Real trade-offs: (1) in-canvas HUD vs header HUD — both can't be primary; (2) silhouette readability vs sky richness — the dino needs a lighter horizon band and larger scale, which means sacrificing some empty sky; (3) crisp retro vs soft atmosphere — the bokeh must go for flat, dithered shapes; (4) one clear jump control vs showing all keys — alternates dilute the primary instruction.
history.suggestion: Prioritized plan (offline, self-contained, no external assets): 1) Restore omitted content first: draw 2–3 flat near-black cactus silhouettes on the foreground ground with rhythmic spacing, and one flying pterodactyl silhouette at duck-height on the right; use the same flat silhouette language as the dino so obstacles read instantly. 2) Make the dino the focal point: scale it ~3–4×, give a crisp mid-stride running pose, a two-tone treatment (near-black body + thin warm rim-light on the sun side) so it separates from the horizon, and align its feet to a confident foreground ground band; raise the dune line so the dino sits against the lighter orange band, not the dark dune. 3) Resolve HUD duplication: keep ONE live SCORE/BEST HUD inside the canvas (top-right, single pixel numeral font, on a subtle dark backing plate for legibility over the sky) and reduce the header to brand + version + BEST only; unify the numeric font across both. 4) Clean the sky for craft: delete the blurry bokeh blobs, replace with 2–3 crisp flat cloud bands (or remove), keep stars small and sharp, and add a faint dither/scanline overlay for the modern-retro signature; tuck the sun partly behind the dune line so it stops competing with the player. 5) Rebuild the ground as 2–3 crisp layered bands (foreground speckled sand, mid dune, far dune) with a hard top edge; restyle the dashed line as subtle sand texture rather than a road. 6) Fix controls: one highlighted primary jump chip (SPACE / ↑ / tap), keep Duck (↓) and Pause, and remove the contradictory 'r Jump' down-arrow chip (or relabel 'R' as Restart); add an in-canvas 'PRESS SPACE TO JUMP' prompt near the dino that fades on first input. 7) Relocate the speed indicator into the in-canvas HUD or attach it to the controls row as 'SPEED 1.0×' with a filled accent bar. 8) Tighten composition: let the viewport dominate the card (trim outer padding), and demote the 'RIPOSA · RUN' text to a low-opacity corner signature. This keeps every required element, makes the dino and a single HUD the clear priorities, unifies the visual system, and gives the scene the rhythmic obstacle spacing and silhouette identity the brief asks for.

history.critique: Brief & Intent: The two explicitly requested gameplay elements — cacti and a flying obstacle — are entirely absent; the playfield is an empty sunset, so the screen reads as a title shell rather than a gameplay screen. The 'clear jump instruction' exists only as a footer legend, not an in-scene prompt, and that legend is self-contradictory (the Jump chip contains both ↑ and ↓ glyphs; the Duck chip labels its key as '↓'). The dino is static with no running pose, so 'running dinosaur' is only nominally fulfilled. Clarity & Hierarchy: Score/best and speed are each duplicated (header BEST + in-game BEST; in-game SPEED + footer SPEED), so there is no single source of truth and the eye bounces between three HUD clusters. The heavy dark in-game HUD box dominates the top-right sky and competes with the scene, while the actual focal subject — the dino — is small, left-of-center, and floats without a contact shadow, leaving the right two-thirds of the frame empty. The low-contrast 'RIPOSA · RUN' watermark adds noise without function. Visual System & Craft: The dino fails the brief's core 'crisp silhouette' test: the body is a dark blob but the legs are two cream stilt-like bars, breaking silhouette unity and reading as a stand rather than legs; the head profile is ambiguous. The gray trapezoid clouds clash with the sunset palette and look like placeholders. The flat ground band's hard top edge cuts across the dune curves, and the dino's feet do not clearly meet the ground line. Two competing component languages exist (outlined footer pills vs. the filled in-game HUD box). Expressiveness: The sunset gradient, sun glow, and RIPOSA wordmark are genuinely distinctive, but with no obstacles, no motion, and a static dino, the scene has no rhythm or memorable gameplay moment; the identity is carried entirely by the chrome, not the game. Real trade-offs: adding cacti/ptero increases density and risks cluttering the clean sky — resolvable by using one shared dark silhouette color for all actors on a consistent baseline with generous rhythmic gaps; consolidating HUDs removes the persistent header best — acceptable since the in-game HUD already shows it; making the dino a single dark color loses the cream accent — acceptable because silhouette readability is the brief's stated priority, with a tiny eye/crest accent retaining identity.
history.suggestion: One prioritized plan: (1) Populate the playfield — place 2–3 cacti of varying heights plus one pterodactyl at duck/jump height across the right two-thirds, all in the same dark silhouette color on the same ground baseline, spaced to a visible rhythm; this restores required content and fixes the empty composition. (2) Redraw the dino as a single-color crisp T-rex silhouette in a mid-stride pose (one leg bent, tail counterweighted), add a soft elliptical contact shadow, and drop the cream stilt legs (keep at most a 1–2px eye/crest accent). (3) Unify the HUD — keep one in-game top-right cluster (SCORE + BEST + small SPEED bar) rendered in the same outlined-pill language as the footer; remove the header BEST pill and the footer speed readout; fix the control chips to Jump = ↑/SPACE and Duck = ↓/S, deleting the stray arrows. (4) Add an in-scene prompt — a centered 'PRESS SPACE TO JUMP' pill (key chip + label) in the sky above the dino, high contrast, satisfying the clear jump instruction. (5) Craft pass — replace the gray clouds with warm/dark-purple silhouettes matching the palette, align the ground top edge with the dino's feet and add a 1px highlight on the ground line, remove the RIPOSA·RUN watermark, and scale the dino up ~15% while keeping the sky clean so the sun glow remains the hero moment.
